blocks.p: Every unstucking practice begins, stays and ends in safety. That doesn't change here. But what if you intentionally allowed more space for safety and defense? What if you allowed your internal experiences of safety and defense to both exist simultaneously?

In [Balancing and Pendulating](piece:balancing-and-pendulating), you deliberately pay attention to safety or defense: safety, then defense, then safety to Balance, and the same repeated at least once to Pendulate.
But you can pay attention to safety and defense. They can both exist in your conscious attention at the same time. You can feel both in your body at the same time.
To Hold and Watch, you need a deep level of safety anchoring. At a deep enough level of anchoring, you can hold both. Once held, you will watch both.

Holding is kind of like a frozen moment in time. You pay attention to both safety and defense as Sensations in your body. You feel where they exist and let them both be there. Of course, you don't reject them or make them be something they aren't. You won't evaluate or judge. You just Hold both within you by choosing to pay attention to them.
To get to the Holding Skill, you will Balance or Pendulate. Once you have both safety and defense within you, you then choose to hold them; to pay attention to them.

When you Balance or Pendulate, there is a definite end to the practice. Once you Balance from defense to safety it's over, right? Same with Pendulation, it's over once you get back to safety. And then you reconnect with the external world and try again when ready.

But Holding has no end to it aside from practical limitations like time, safety state capacity, and interruptions. Otherwise, after you Balance or Pendulate, you can then Hold as long as you like. If you plan to practice at this level, please ensure you have lots of space, peace, freedom to move, and a [Passive Safety Environment](piece:anchor-environment) that is ready for you.
You could Hold at any depth of A→W→E, but you will get the deepest, purest, and most self-regulatory result from Describing Sensations at the Experiencing level.
"Why would I Hold, Justin?"
Because of what might happen next.
Watching is remaining open to what may happen next as a result of Holding.

Your body is always compelled to self-regulate, right? It's a living biological organism always wanting to reach homeostasis and optimize its resources. So, when you Watch what you're Holding, you patiently wait for the body to maybe self-regulate at a deeper, Received level. (I say "maybe" because it's not a guarantee.) As Received self-regulation begins, you can Watch it and see where it takes you.
By this point, you're Holding safety and defense. Now, you Watch the two at the same time. And you wait to see what happens, if anything. The two may want to interact in some way... or not.

If you're Holding & Watching at the Experiencing level, you have the opportunity to watch fully-formed Sensations within you as they interact with each other. But what happens at this point is out of your direct control.

blocks.why: Holding asks for a deep anchor. This practice is where that anchor starts.

blocks.p: Holding & Watching are the final two skills, transitioning you from Active self-regulation to Received self-regulation. What may happen next is in [Received self-regulation](piece:received-self-regulation).
With all the skills learned ([Cue to Anchor](piece:cue-to-anchor) through Holding & Watching), the main work is consistent, dedicated practice. Focus on:

ul: Practicing the skills based on capacity
Gradually increasing the depth at which you practice (Anchored Awareness, then Witnessing, then Experiencing)
Working with progressively deeper layers of stuck defense as capacity builds

blocks.p: As you practice over weeks and months, Received Self-Regulation will open naturally. You cannot force or rush this phase. It emerges when your nervous system is ready.
A reminder for the journey:

ul: SSIEC is what you find along the way.
The skills are what you need to progress.

blocks.p: Keep practicing and progressing little by little.
